From an idea to a visual plan.

A browser-based design tool for kitchens, fitted bedrooms and stairs, bringing layouts, component dimensions and materials into a visual workspace.

Joinery Studio

01 / The project

What it is

Joinery Studio is an interactive planning app for kitchens, fitted bedrooms and stairs. It is intended to support a showroom conversation: turn an idea into a visual layout, adjust the design and discuss it with the customer.

The audience is joinery designers and showroom staff working with customers. The workspace supports early design exploration and communication; it is not presented as a replacement for manufacturing drawings or production approval.

02 / The challenge

What it needs to solve

A design tool has to connect visual changes with meaningful dimensions. It also needs to guide users into the right type of space, so a kitchen, bedroom and staircase do not all begin with the same generic setup.

03 / Design thinking

The approach

The opening journey uses Space, Layout and Room steps. Kitchen, Bedroom and Stairs are visible choices from the start, giving the user a recognisable route into the task before entering the design workspace.

The application combines a millimetre-based geometry model with component dimensions, materials and different views. Its Next.js and TypeScript codebase also includes undo and redo, JSON backups, revision snapshots and drawing export. These support iteration rather than treating the first layout as a final answer.

04 / The experience

How it works

  1. Start with a real space

    Choose Kitchen, Bedroom or Stairs, then work through the layout and room setup.

  2. Develop the design

    Arrange the joinery components and adjust dimensions and materials, using the available views to inspect the layout.

  3. Review and share

    Use revisions and export tools to support a design discussion and retain a record of the proposed layout.

The goal is a practical conversation tool: help the designer and customer compare ideas visually, understand the proposed space and agree what needs further development.
